claims: Agentic coding means you review code more than write it, so the diff viewer needs jump-to-definition and find-references, which Conductor's plain viewer lacked
The whole Conductor parallel-agent experience can be rebuilt in a terminal with worktrees plus neovim
conductor-setup.sh pulls env vars from the parent local environment and from the cloud, then runs pnpm install and pnpm build
Agent-first terminals (Warp, 'Sea Monkeys') let you spin up multiple workspaces/agents in parallel
how_to_steps: Write a script (yw <branch>) that: replaces spaces with hyphens, fetches origin main, creates a git worktree in a base dir on a new branch from origin/main, cds into it

Have it run a setup script that copies gitignored env files (packages/supabase/.env.local, packages/resend/.env.local) and config dirs (apps/yorby-web/.vercel) from the root repo, then pnpm install && pnpm build
End the script by launching claude
Configure Warp so a new tab runs the script in a left pane and Claude Code in the right pane
After Claude edits, open neovim: space gs for changed files, space hd for side-by-side diff, grd/grr for definition/references, space do for diffview.nvim
on_screen_only: Conductor web UI with 'Download Conductor' button and a workspace diff summary

Script source: '# Replace spaces with hyphens', 'local worktree_path="$YORBY_WORKTREE_BASE/$branch"', 'git -C "$YORBY_MAIN_REPO" fetch origin main', 'git worktree add "$worktree_path" -b "$branch" origin/main', '../scripts/conductor-setup.sh', 'claude'

Setup script: ENV_FILES list ('packages/supabase/.env.local', 'packages/resend/.env.local'), CONFIG_DIRS ('apps/yorby-web/.vercel', 'apps/yorby-admin-web/.vercel'), echo 'Copying env files from root repo...', 'Copying config directories (e.g. .vercel) from root repo...', COPIED/SKIPPED counters
Warp split: left pane 'New terminal session' running setup, right pane Claude Code banner
neovim side-by-side diff of photo-library-panel.tsx with updateTitleMutation / useMutation changes
cta: watch the linked long-form neovim + Claude Code setup video

relevance.why: Parallel worktree sessions with a one-command bootstrap (env copy + install + launch claude) is directly useful for running several Claude Code agents on Haji's apps. The neovim half is a developer preference, not a time saver for a time-poor founder.

implement_score.why: Port the worktree + setup script idea (30 minutes per repo) so each parallel Claude session starts with env and deps ready; skip neovim and use whatever diff viewer is already at hand.

gap.what: Liked set has no parallel-worktree bootstrap or diff-review workflow; adds the worktree script pattern, env/config copying from the root repo, Warp launch configs, Conductor as a reference tool, and diffview.nvim.
